rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline is competitive and what performance floor to expect. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA representation without aggregation or fusion. It is the best next experiment because it is cheap, interpretable, and establishes a reference point for later comparisons of RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is a modest RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline (accuracy 0.4849, F1 0.4639), leaving large uncertainty about whether image features are useful at all. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the modality choice with a simple unimodal model and no aggregation or fusion confounds. This is the best next experiment because it establishes the image performance reference needed to decide whether to exploit image/multimodal directions or focus on RNA representation and profile choices, while avoiding premature testing of more complex multimodal configurations.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile in both accuracy and F1, so RNA is the promising modality. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder improves over PCA. config_004 tests scvi_n200 with the same singleprofile setting and no aggregation, isolating the RNA representation choice. This is the best next use of budget because it is a clean one-variable comparison on the stronger modality, avoids assuming multiprofile or multimodal complexity will help, and will inform whether subsequent experiments should build on scvi or remain PCA-based.

The strongest completed result is config_004, an RNA-only singleprofile model with scvi_n200, which outperforms PCA RNA and image-only ResNet50 in both accuracy and F1. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve this promising RNA representation. config_005 tests that directly by keeping model setting, RNA encoder, and modality fixed while changing from singleprofile to multiprofile with the simplest aggregation, avgpool. This isolates the profile/aggregation effect without introducing fusion or a new image encoder, making it the most informative next step under a limited budget.

The strongest result so far is config_005, but it is a single experiment showing a large jump from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool using scvi. This leaves uncertainty about whether the gain is due to multiprofile aggregation generally or is specific to the scvi encoder. config_002 tests the same multiprofile avgpool setting with pca_n2000, completing a clean encoder-by-profile comparison with config_001 and config_005. This is the best next use of budget because it isolates the profile/aggregation effect before adding further complexity such as transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile models are currently strongest, with scvi_n200 + avgpool outperforming both singleprofile RNA and pca-based multiprofile. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for the best RNA encoder. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer relative to the current best, isolating that design choice while exploiting the most promising direction.

RNA multiprofile models are much stronger than single-profile baselines, and scvi_n200 currently outperforms pca_n2000 for both single-profile and multiprofile avgpool settings. However, the transformer aggregation gain over avgpool is small for scvi, so it is unclear whether aggregation matters generally or only interacts with the encoder. config_003 tests pca_n2000 with multiprofile and transformer aggregation, directly comparing to config_002 for aggregation and to config_006 for encoder choice. This is the best next experiment because it completes the simple RNA-only 2x2 comparison, isolates important representation and aggregation effects without adding multimodal complexity, and helps decide which RNA setting to use before testing fusion.

RNA multiprofile scvi_n200 is currently the strongest direction (accuracy ~0.65, F1 ~0.63), but image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is weak (accuracy 0.208, F1 0.172), leaving uncertainty about whether image can contribute at all or whether the poor score is due to singleprofile/no aggregation. config_011 keeps the image encoder fixed and adds multiprofile avgpool, directly testing the profile/aggregation effect for image without introducing RNA or fusion. This is a minimal, high-information step before committing to multimodal ResNet50 fusion: if image improves, multimodal becomes more attractive; if not, ResNet50-based multimodal can be deprioritized.

The strongest evidence is RNA multiprofile with scvi_n200 (0.650 avgpool, 0.653 transformer; F1 supports), while PCA is lower and image-only ResNet is weak. scgpt is untested, so there is uncertainty about RNA representation. config_008 tests scgpt under the same multiprofile/avgpool setting, isolating the encoder effect without adding fusion or relying on the tiny transformer advantage. This is a simple, high-value extension of the promising RNA direction, can improve the current best baseline, and clarifies whether encoder choice matters before investing in multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation is the strongest baseline (config_006, acc 0.653, F1 0.628), slightly ahead of avgpool and much ahead of pca or scgpt variants. Image-only ResNet is weak (config_011, acc 0.328), so the key uncertainty is whether adding image features to the best RNA representation improves validation accuracy. config_032 extends config_006 by adding the already-baselined ResNet image encoder with simple concat fusion while keeping the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed. This directly tests the contribution of the image modality relative to the best RNA-only model and is a focused, high-value next step before testing more complex fusion or stronger image encoders.
